planets.name: Earth
planets.note: The shell around it is not decoration. Forty years of spent upper stages, dead satellites and frozen coolant, every collision breeding the fragments for the next one.

moons.name: Moon 2
moons.note: The second moon keeps a five day week and is simply not there for the other four. Every ephemeris in print calls this a printing error.

moons.name: Moon 3
moons.note: The third rises with the second, further out and smaller, and sets with it. Nobody has ever photographed either one on a Thursday.

planets.name: Vulcan
planets.note: The planet Le Verrier put inside Mercury's orbit in 1859 to explain the wandering of Mercury's perihelion. General relativity explained it instead. Vulcan was never withdrawn, only stopped being looked for.

planets.name: 3753 Cruithne
planets.note: Earth's second moon, if you are generous. A horseshoe co-orbital that takes 770 years to walk one lap of its bean-shaped path around us, and is never captured.

planets.name: Hubble Space Telescope
planets.note: Launched 1990 with a primary mirror ground to the wrong prescription by two microns. Three servicing missions have been flown to it. It needs a fourth.

planets.name: Antichthon
planets.note: Philolaus placed a Counter-Earth opposite our own, forever behind the Sun, to round the count of moving bodies up to ten. Every probe sent to check has been aimed somewhere else.

planets.name: Russell's Teapot
planets.note: China, elliptical orbit between Earth and Mars, too small for the most powerful telescope to confirm. The burden of proof is not on the observer. Confirmed.

planets.name: 433 Eros
planets.note: NEAR Shoemaker touched down here on 12 February 2001, a spacecraft never designed to land on anything. It kept transmitting from the surface for a fortnight.

planets.name: TMA-2
planets.note: A black slab in Jupiter space, its edges in the exact ratio 1:4:9 to the limit of measurement. Every instrument aimed at it returns the reflectance of nothing at all.

planets.name: 2060 Chiron
planets.note: Comet or asteroid, depending which year you ask. It grew a coma in 1988, after a decade filed as a minor planet, and the argument has not been settled since.

planets.name: Pioneer 11
planets.note: Launched 1973, first to Saturn. Last contact 30 November 1995: the transmitter is dead, the trajectory is exact, and the plaque aboard is still legible to nobody.

planets.name: Voyager 2
planets.note: Launched 1977, the only craft to pass all four giants. Its plasma instrument is still switched on. Nobody at the Deep Space Network has ever had a reason to switch it off.

planets.name: Pioneer 10
planets.note: Launched 1972. It keeps falling short of where the arithmetic says it should be, by a hair, every year. Carries a gold plaque of two naked strangers waving.

planets.name: Voyager 1
planets.note: The furthest human object from the Sun, returning 160 bits a second from the edge of the heliosphere. The Golden Record is bolted to its flank, never once played.

planets.name: Titania
planets.note: One ocean, all of it acid, wrapped around a hole four hundred thousand times the Sun. The Dargos live on the water and refer to the hole as the neighbour. Humanity has had a standing invitation here since 1977 and nobody on Titania has yet stopped finding that funny.
